content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The core restructuring is clean and idiomatic: `OwnerHousehold` stays the single source of truth with a tidy `idFor(lastName, postcode)` + two typed `deriveId` overloads, `AssignHousehold` collapses to the one thing it still needs to do, and each step reads `sharesHousehold` for its own distinct decision (bypass hard-dup vs. skip soft-dup flag) rather than sharing mutable state. That all reads naturally.

One coherence defect the diff leaves behind, though:

**Stale contract doc in `OwnerAddress.java` (lines 14–17).** This change severs `OwnerHousehold`'s dependency on address normalisation — the household is now keyed on `(lastName, postcode)` and `OwnerHousehold` no longer calls `OwnerAddress.normalize` at all. But `OwnerAddress`'s class javadoc still advertises that consumer:

> "Centralised here … so every site agrees on one definition: `ValidateOwnerFields` stores the canonical value …, while **`OwnerHousehold` compares the canonical value for duplicate detection and the shared household id.**"

That second clause is now false. `OwnerAddress` bills itself as the "single source of truth … used across the `POST /owners` pipeline" and enumerates its call sites, so a maintainer will trust that list — and here it names a consumer that no longer exists. Since `OwnerAddress` is now used only by `ValidateOwnerFields` (address storage/blank-rejection), the javadoc should drop the `OwnerHousehold` reference (and reconsider whether "duplicate detection" still belongs in its stated purpose at all). The `@link` to `OwnerHousehold` was part of what made these two files cohere; removing the dependency without updating the doc breaks that.

Everything else — the pipeline wiring, the two-case guard in `CheckOwnerIdentityUnique`, and the OpenAI/OpenAPI description updates — is consistent with the new household model.
